questions.question: The International Date Line passes through which of the following oceans?
questions.explanation: The International Date Line roughly follows the 180° meridian and passes primarily through the Pacific Ocean, deviating in some places to accommodate certain island groups and territories.

questions.question: The 'Sun Temple' at Konark, a UNESCO World Heritage Site built in the shape of a giant chariot with twelve pairs of wheels, is dedicated to which Hindu deity?
questions.explanation: The Konark Sun Temple, built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, is dedicated to Surya, the Sun God. Its architecture represents a colossal chariot with 24 wheels drawn by seven horses.

questions.question: The 'Sangai' dancing deer, an endemic and endangered subspecies of Eld's deer found only in India, is the state animal of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii), also known as the dancing deer of Manipur, is found exclusively in the Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world, located on Loktak Lake in Manipur.

questions.question: The 'Kalamkari' art form, known for its intricate hand-painted or block-printed cotton textiles depicting mythological scenes, is primarily associated with which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kalamkari, literally meaning 'pen work,' is primarily associated with Andhra Pradesh, specifically the Machilipatnam and Srikalahasti styles. The art form uses natural dyes and involves 23 steps of dyeing and painting.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the right to constitutional remedies, enabling citizens to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: Article 32 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to constitutional remedies. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution, as it empowers citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of their fundamental rights.

questions.question: The 'Bishnupriya Manipuri' language, which has been demanding inclusion in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, belongs to which language family?
questions.explanation: Bishnupriya Manipuri is an Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in parts of Assam, Manipur, and Tripura. It evolved from Magadhi Prakrit with significant influences from Bengali and Assamese, and is distinct from the Meitei language of Manipur.

questions.question: The 'Moplah' (or Malabar) rebellion of 1921, an armed uprising against British authorities and local Hindu landlords, took place in which region of India?
questions.explanation: The Moplah Rebellion of 1921 was an armed uprising by Muslim Mappila peasants against British colonial authorities and Hindu landlords in the Malabar region of Kerala. It was part of the broader Khilafat and Non-Cooperation movements.

questions.question: The Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were merged into a single Union Territory in which year?
questions.explanation: The Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were merged into a single Union Territory named 'Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu' on 26 January 2020 through an Act of Parliament.

questions.question: The 'PM Gati Shakti' scheme, a national master plan for multi-modal connectivity infrastructure, was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: PM Gati Shakti, the National Master Plan for Multi-modal Connectivity, was launched on 13 October 2021. It aims to bring together 16 ministries on a single digital platform for integrated planning and coordinated implementation of infrastructure projects.

questions.question: The 47th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee, where India's Santiniketan was inscribed as a World Heritage Site, was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The 47th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee was held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in September 2023. During this session, Santiniketan, established by Rabindranath Tagore, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: The 'Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen)' Phase 2, aimed at achieving ODF Plus status for all villages, was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase 2 was launched in 2020-21 with the goal of achieving ODF Plus status for all villages by 2024-25, focusing on sustainability of ODF status and solid and liquid waste management.

questions.question: The 'PM Kisan Samman Nidhi' scheme provides annual financial assistance of how much to eligible farmer families?
questions.explanation: The PM Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme provides ₹6,000 per year to eligible landholding farmer families, payable in three equal installments of ₹2,000 every four months, directly into their bank accounts via DBT.

questions.question: The 'Khelo India' initiative, aimed at promoting sports at the grassroots level and identifying young talent, was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: The Khelo India programme was launched in 2018 with the aim of building a robust sports ecosystem in India. It focuses on grassroots development, talent identification, and promotion of sports across the country through various competitions and infrastructure development.

questions.question: The 'Sagar Mala' project, aimed at promoting port-led development and modernizing India's port infrastructure, was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: The Sagar Mala project was launched in 2015 with the vision of developing India's coastline and maritime sector. It aims to modernize port infrastructure, improve connectivity, and promote port-led direct and indirect development.

questions.question: The 'Vande Bharat' train service, India's first semi-high-speed train, was first flagged off between which two cities?
questions.explanation: India's first Vande Bharat Express was flagged off on 15 February 2019 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, running between New Delhi and Varanasi. It was the first semi-high-speed train designed and manufactured entirely in India under the 'Make in India' initiative.

questions.question: If 'P' denotes 'multiplied by', 'Q' denotes 'divided by', 'R' denotes 'added to', and 'S' denotes 'subtracted from', then the value of 18 Q 3 P 5 R 6 S 4 is:
questions.explanation: Substituting the symbols: 18 ÷ 3 × 5 + 6 − 4 = 6 × 5 + 6 − 4 = 30 + 6 − 4 = 32. Following BODMAS, division and multiplication are performed left to right before addition and subtraction.

questions.question: In a row of students, Amit is 18th from the left end and 23rd from the right end. How many students are there in the row?
questions.explanation: Total students = (Position from left) + (Position from right) − 1 = 18 + 23 − 1 = 40. We subtract 1 because Amit is counted twice.

questions.question: Select the missing number from the given responses: 2, 9, 28, 65, 126, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern follows n³ + 1: 1³+1=2, 2³+1=9, 3³+1=28, 4³+1=65, 5³+1=126, 6³+1=217. The next term is 6³ + 1 = 217.

questions.question: A number is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change?
questions.explanation: Let the number be 100. After 20% increase: 120. After 20% decrease: 120 × 0.8 = 96. Net change = 100 − 96 = 4% decrease. This is because the 20% decrease is applied to a larger base (120).

questions.question: If A + B means A is the sister of B, A − B means A is the brother of B, and A × B means A is the mother of B, then what does the expression P × Q + R − S indicate?
options: A) P is the grandmother of S
B) P is the mother of R's brother
C) P is the mother of R and R is the brother of S
D) P is the mother of S
questions.explanation: P × Q means P is the mother of Q. Q + R means Q is the sister of R. R − S means R is the brother of S. Thus P is the mother of Q (sister of R) and R (brother of S), meaning P is the mother of R and R is the brother of S.

questions.question: In a family, A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. C is the mother of D. D is the brother of E. E is the father of F. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: A is father of B and C (B is sister of C). C is mother of D and E (D is brother of E). E is father of F. So A → C (daughter) → E (son) → F. A is the great-grandfather of F.

questions.question: In a certain code, '256' means 'you are good', '634' means 'good and bad', and '357' means 'bad is evil'. Which digit stands for 'bad'?
questions.explanation: From '634' (good and bad) and '357' (bad is evil), both share digit '3' and the word 'bad'. Therefore, digit 3 stands for 'bad'.

questions.question: What is 15% of 240?
The ratio of the ages of A and B is 4:5. If the sum of their ages is 54 years, what is the age of B?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 4x and 5x. Then 4x + 5x = 54 → 9x = 54 → x = 6. Age of B = 5x = 5 × 6 = 30 years.

questions.question: A trader bought an article for ₹600 and sold it at a loss of 20%. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 - Loss%) = 600 × 0.80 = ₹480. Alternatively, Loss = 20% of 600 = ₹120, so SP = 600 - 120 = ₹480.

questions.question: If a train covers 480 km in 6 hours, what is its speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: Speed = Distance / Time = 480 km / 6 hours = 80 km/h.

questions.question: A man rows upstream at 8 km/h and downstream at 12 km/h. What is the speed of the man in still water?
questions.explanation: Speed in still water = (Upstream speed + Downstream speed) / 2 = (8 + 12) / 2 = 10 km/h. The stream speed would be (12 − 8) / 2 = 2 km/h.

questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹15,000 at 8% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 23. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: Let the 5 consecutive odd numbers be n, n+2, n+4, n+6, n+8. Their average = (5n + 20)/5 = n + 4 = 23 → n = 19. The numbers are 19, 21, 23, 25, 27. The largest is 27.

questions.question: If the cost of 12 pens is ₹180, what is the cost of 8 pens?
questions.explanation: Cost per pen = 180/12 = ₹15. Cost of 8 pens = 8 × 15 = ₹120.

questions.question: The area of a rectangle is 120 cm² and its length is 15 cm. What is its breadth?
questions.explanation: Breadth = Area / Length = 120 / 15 = 8 cm.

questions.question: A sum of money triples itself in 8 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: If P triples to 3P, then SI = 2P. Using SI = PRT/100: 2P = P × R × 8/100 → R = 200/8 = 25% per annum.

questions.question: A survey found that 30% of respondents prefer tea over coffee. If 420 respondents prefer tea, how many were surveyed?
questions.explanation: 30% of total = 420. Total = 420 / 0.30 = 1400 respondents.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 20 days. B can do it in 30 days. They work together for 6 days and then A leaves. How many more days will B take to finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: A's 1-day work = 1/20, B's 1-day work = 1/30. Together = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12. In 6 days, they complete 6/12 = 1/2 of the work. Remaining work = 1/2. B alone will take (1/2)/(1/30) = 15 days.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above the cost price and gives a discount of 20%. What is his profit percentage?
Two trains of lengths 200 m and 300 m are running at speeds of 72 km/h and 54 km/h respectively in opposite directions. How long will they take to cross each other?
questions.explanation: Total distance to cover = 200 + 300 = 500 m. Relative speed = 72 + 54 = 126 km/h = 126 × (5/18) = 35 m/s. Time = Distance/Speed = 500/35 = 14.28 seconds.

questions.question: Find the missing letter in the series: A, D, G, J, M, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern adds 3 positions each time: A(1)→D(4)→G(7)→J(10)→M(13)→P(16). Each letter is 3 positions ahead of the previous one.

questions.question: In a certain code, 'BANANA' is written as 'CBOBOB' (each letter replaced by the next letter in the alphabet). How is 'PAPAYA' written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Applying the same rule: P→Q, A→B, P→Q, A→B, Y→Z, A→B. Thus PAPAYA becomes QBQBZB.

questions.question: Select the related word from the given alternatives: Sculptor : Statue :: Poet : ?
questions.explanation: A sculptor creates a statue; similarly, a poet creates a poem. The relationship is creator to creation.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S, T, and V are six teachers. Q is younger than R but older than P. S is younger than T but older than Q. V is younger than P. Who is the youngest among all?
questions.explanation: From the statements: R > Q > P > V and T > S > Q. Combining: T > S > Q > P > V. V is younger than everyone else, making V the youngest.

questions.question: Find the odd one out from the given pairs of numbers:
questions.explanation: Pairs A (3,5), B (5,7), and C (11,13) are all twin primes — pairs of prime numbers that differ by exactly 2. Pair D (7,11) has a difference of 4, so it is not a twin prime pair.

questions.question: In a certain code, 'DELHI' is written as 'CFKGF' (alternating pattern: −1, +1, −1, +1, −1). How is 'MUMBAI' written using the same pattern?
questions.explanation: M−1=L, U+1=V, M−1=L, B+1=C, A−1=Z, I+1=H. So MUMBAI = LVLCZH.

questions.question: Five people — P, Q, R, S, T — are sitting in a row facing north. P is to the left of Q. R is to the right of P but to the left of S. T is to the right of S. Who is sitting at the extreme right?
questions.explanation: From the constraints: P < Q, P < R < S, and S < T. Combining: P < R < S < T, with Q somewhere to the right of P. Regardless of Q's exact position, T is always at the extreme right.

questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting and is often given to newborns to prevent hemorrhagic disease?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of clotting factors (prothrombin, factors VII, IX, and X) in the liver. Newborns are often given a Vitamin K injection at birth to prevent Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding (VKDB).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen (N₂), which constitutes about 78% of Earth's atmosphere, is not a greenhouse gas because it does not absorb infrared radiation. CO₂, methane, and water vapor are all significant greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere.

questions.question: The process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy in the form of glucose is called:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy (usually from the sun) into chemical energy stored in glucose. The overall equation is 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary cause of acid rain?
options: A) Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides
questions.explanation: Acid rain is primarily caused by sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) released from burning fossil fuels. These gases react with water vapor in the atmosphere to form sulfuric acid and nitric acid, which fall as acid rain.

questions.question: The 'Biodiversity Hotspot' concept, which identifies regions with exceptional concentrations of endemic species experiencing significant habitat loss, was first proposed by which scientist?
questions.explanation: The concept of biodiversity hotspots was first proposed by British ecologist Norman Myers in 1988. A biodiversity hotspot must contain at least 1,500 endemic plant species and have lost at least 70% of its original habitat.

questions.question: The 'Blue Baby' syndrome (methemoglobinemia) in infants is caused by the presence of which of the following in drinking water?
questions.explanation: Blue Baby syndrome (methemoglobinemia) is caused by high levels of nitrates in drinking water. Nitrates are converted to nitrites in the body, which oxidize hemoglobin to methemoglobin, reducing its oxygen-carrying capacity and causing cyanosis (bluish discoloration) in infants.

questions.question: The 'Green Revolution' in India, which transformed the country from a food-deficit to a food-surplus nation, was primarily based on the introduction of high-yielding varieties of which crop first?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution in India, spearheaded by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, began in the mid-1960s with the introduction of high-yielding varieties (HYV) of wheat, particularly the dwarf varieties developed by Norman Borlaug. Wheat was the first crop to benefit, followed by rice.
